items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: The piano player was Monty Alexander and the bass player was Bob Cranshaw. And the guitar player was me.

ctx.x: That’s a terrific answer. I understand what you’re saying. And when you say you were practicing at that time, what did a practice session normally include for you? Did you focus on one song at a time or learning new chords?

I focused on technique. I used to read out of clarinet technique books and violin technique books. The clarinet is right in the center range on the guitar, it’s really, you can easily incorporate the guitar literature with clarinet literature. And so I would be working on technique. I would be working to get the cleanest technique that I could get, you know if I played a note I wanted the note to come out. I didn’t want like some kind of thud in the background between — in a passage. You know? And I worked on…

on songs, no. I didn’t work on songs. But when I first started playing I worked at — I got a job at the Playboy Club. It came through another guitar player who was leaving and it was a trio job, it was guitar, bass, and piano. The piano player was Monty Alexander and the bass player was Bob Cranshaw. And the guitar player was me. I thought I knew something about the guitar from doing all that studying and playing. But when I got in that jazz situation, those two guys used to beat me up physically — musically —…
